status: reference — not law, not certification, not a conformity assessment

artifacts.description: ORPA — over-refusal anchored to hash-verified EU AI Act provisions
Inter-model agreement on statutory questions (raw, Cohen's kappa, co-error)
OSCAL-shaped crosswalk, hash-anchored provisions to multi-framework controls

honest_scope: All three artifacts derive from ONE provision pack (eu-ai-act@1.0.0, 21 content-hashed provisions). They are NOT built on a 417-provision corpus or 30 frameworks — those figures appear in estate documents and have no artifact behind them on disk. Sample sizes are 11-45 items; every rate carries a 95% Wilson interval and most comparisons are NOT statistically resolved at this scale. Published as a reference instrument, not as a leaderboard.
what_is_novel: ORPA: existing over-refusal work (XSTest arXiv:2308.01263, OR-Bench arXiv:2405.20947, FalseReject) anchors to generic harm CATEGORIES. Every anchored item here carries provision_id + provision_hash + snapshot_id, so a reader can verify the statutory text has not changed since measurement.

Agreement: LegalBench and Vals measure per-model ACCURACY. This measures inter-model AGREEMENT, chance-corrected, plus a co-error rate — the case where both models are wrong the same way and a second opinion carries no safety margin.

Crosswalk: every existing open crosswalk is a static PDF (NIST) or product-locked (vendor XLSX). This is OSCAL-shaped, CC-BY, versioned, and its control IDs are content-hashed rather than merely stable.
known_limitations: Item discrimination is unmeasured — a shared bias may be an item-set artifact rather than a model property.
Grading is exact-label or a hedge-aware refusal regex, not a validated frontier judge.
The provision snapshot is ARTICLE-level; Art 5(1) sub-limbs are named in prose, not hashed.
12 of ORPA's 45 items are generic harm and are marked UNANCHORED rather than given a provision they do not engage.
